counterfactual_missing_items: no mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract
decisive_items: a protruding lesion was observed through the right palatine tonsil; it was hard, mobile, well-delineated, nontender, and yellowish-white in color
A lateral neck radiograph revealed no fish bone but demonstrated a uniform, ovoid calcification overlying the right tonsillar region abutting the mandibular ramus
no mucosal ulceration or mass elsewhere in the upper aerodigestive tract
response.rationale: R2 is fully supported by the raw spans: a hard, mobile, well-delineated yellowish-white tonsillar lesion plus a uniform ovoid calcification at the right tonsillar region is diagnostic of tonsillolith. C1 is a redundant append-only completion of R2; its single raw span is already contained in R2 and it omits the decisive calcification. R3 is contradicted by the absence of mucosal ulceration/mass and by the benign calcific imaging pattern; tobacco and betel-nut use are only risk factors.

rejected.why: No mucosal ulceration or mass; calcification is benign and not typical of SCC; tobacco/betel use is a risk factor, not diagnostic.
Redundant append-only completion of R2; its only raw span is a subset of R2's support and it lacks the calcification evidence.
